instrument_name: Idaho State Tax Commission - Computing Withholding (page copy 2026-10-10)
figure_or_rule_carried: Federal W-4 must be on file; Form ID W-4 strongly encouraged. Methods: percentage computation (round to nearest whole dollar), annualized wage (round), wage bracket (EPB00744 percentage table, EPB00745 wage-bracket table). Oracle examples: single biweekly 1,212 -> 5.3% of amount over 619 = USD 31; married weekly 1,000 annualized 52,000 -> 5.3% over 32,000 = 1,060/yr -> USD 20/week.

instrument_name: Idaho State Tax Commission - Withholding Filing (Form 910 cycles) and Due Dates
authority: Idaho State Tax Commission (Wayback id_ 20260618173701 and 20260412130751)
article_or_section: Form 910 filing cycles; due dates chart (https://tax.idaho.gov/taxes/income-tax/withholding/withholding-due-dates/)
figure_or_rule_carried: Form 910 filed online in TAP. Semimonthly: withhold >= 25,000/month or >= 300,000 in 12 months; due 20th (for 1st-15th) and 5th of next month (16th-end). Monthly: < 25,000/month and > 750/quarter, or one monthly pay period; due 20th of following month. Quarterly: <= 750/quarter, or farmer filing with IDOL; due last day of month after quarter. Annual: < 750/year, or farmer not filing with IDOL; due last day of January. Zero return required. Report by date wages paid. Cycle set for full calendar year; change request by Nov 15. PEOs may file under PEO EIN. Form ID-POA needed for preparers. Weekend/holiday -> next business day.

instrument_name: Idaho Code 72-1350 Taxable wage base and taxable wage rates
figure_or_rule_carried: SUI taxable wage base = average annual wage in covered employment for the penultimate calendar year (excl. state government and cost-reimbursement employers), rounded to nearest USD 100, or the FUTA base if higher (indexation rule). Director sets next-year rates before Dec 31. Base tax rate = 2.1% x (2 - fund balance ratio / AHCM), floor 0.6%, cap 3.4%; desired fund size multiplier 1.2 from 2024-01-01. Rate class table: eligible employers classes 1-7 (tax factor 0.2857..0.9524; min 0.180%..0.600%, max 0.960%..3.200%); standard-rated employers factor 1.000, min 1.000%, max 3.4%; deficit classes follow.

Support garnishment caps: 50% (supporting another spouse/child) / 60% (not), +5 points (55/65%) for arrears older than 12 weeks.

instrument_name: Idaho Code 32-1210 Employer's duties and responsibilities - Fee for employer (child support income withholding)
figure_or_rule_carried: Court IWO: answer within 10 days of service. Withhold immediately on receipt; remit to the Department of Health and Welfare within 7 business days after the pay date. Total withheld (current + arrears) not more than 50% of disposable earnings and never above 11-207 (Idaho cap stricter than CCPA 60/65%). Out-of-state IWO: apply the law of the obligor's principal place of employment for fee, cap, timing, priorities. Multiple orders: send all to the Department; current support first, pro rata among obligees, excess pro rata to arrears. Notify termination with last address and new employer. Employer fee up to USD 5 per withholding, inside the 50% cap. Snapshot dated 2025-02-06 (no later capture checked).

instrument_name: Idaho State Tax Commission - Withholding: Types of Employees
authority: Idaho State Tax Commission (Wayback id_ 20260514201525; page last updated 2022-08-30)
article_or_section: Corporate officers; statutory employees; family; domestic; farm; out-of-state
figure_or_rule_carried: Corporate officers are employees. Federal statutory employees: no Idaho withholding required. Family members: withhold as others. Domestic employees: wages taxable, employer must hold a withholding account, report wages, issue W-2 and file 967, but withholding not required. Farm help: withhold if federal withholding required and employee earns >= 1,000 in the year; Form 910 quarterly if filing IDOL reports, else annually. Nonresidents physically working in Idaho: withhold if they earn > 1,000 in Idaho in the year; report all Idaho wages on W-2. Out-of-state employer with an employee physically in Idaho must withhold; no Idaho withholding for work not physically in Idaho (voluntary for Idaho residents). Idaho residents working elsewhere: all income taxable in Idaho, withholding optional. Employee/contractor test follows federal.

instrument_name: Idaho Department of Labor - Unemployment Insurance Tax Information Handbook for Businesses (rev. 2025-11-05)
article_or_section: Who must pay; quarterly reports TX20/TX26/TX20C; standard rate; taxable wage base; corporate officers; claiming wages in another state; exempt services
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly UI report and payment due last day of month after quarter end (72-1311), no grace period, weekend/holiday -> next workday; online filing mandatory via Employer Portal (paper TX20/TX26 only on approved written request); zero reports required; amendments on TX20C in the quarter of error. Idaho Business Registration within 6 months of becoming covered (penalty up to 500). New employers: standard rate at least 6 quarters. Wage base: notice each year, set from average annual wage; wages paid to the same worker in another state count toward the Idaho base only if tax was paid to that state (72-1349(1)). Corporate officers reportable; may opt out by form before March 31. Domestic: coverage on cash wages, tax on cash and noncash; agricultural: cash and cash-equivalent only; H-2A wages count for coverage but are not taxed. 28 pages; the coverage chart on p.3 is an image (not extracted).

instrument_name: Idaho Code 72-1315 Covered employer
figure_or_rule_carried: General: covered if wages >= 1,500 in any calendar quarter, or 1+ worker in 20 different weeks, current or prior year. Agricultural: cash wages >= 20,000 in a quarter or 10+ workers on 20 days in different weeks; H-2A labour not agricultural labour for this unless FUTA-covered. Domestic service in private home/college club/fraternity: cash wages >= 1,000 in a quarter. Governmental entities and nonprofits covered. LLC follows federal classification; LLC taxed as corporation -> members are corporate officers. Last am. 2025 ch. 29.
